title: refactor-stream-aggregator-and-sessioncache-contracts
creator: Marcus Liu
description:
Summary: This ticket tackles long-standing tech debt in the runtime's streaming aggregation path and the in-memory session state store. The current coalescer and session cache are tightly coupled, rely on a mix of spinlocks and coarse-grained mutexes, and make scheduler logic brittle under heterogeneous load patterns. We will introduce a minimal StreamingAggregator abstraction, stabilize the session-cache eviction contract, and simplify the dispatcher/scheduler handoff to reduce contention and improve tail latency.

Goals:
- Replace ad-hoc coalescing logic with a scoped StreamingAggregator that exposes a stable API for prefix/KV cache prefetching and commit semantics.
- Define a sessioncache contract (read-through, pinned hot keys, epoched eviction) to decouple lifecycle from the coalescer.
- Move to an epoch-based, lock-reduced slot handoff for ingress->scheduler to reduce contention under high concurrency.
- Keep API backwards-compatible for model adapters and avoid changes to public REST/SDK surface.
- Add regression tests, perf benchmarks, and observability for rollout decisions.

Proposed approach/Implementation notes:
1) StreamingAggregator abstraction: a slim adapter that handles request grouping and exposes per-window commit callbacks. It will live behind an interface used by the ingress and by the scheduler. This replaces the current "continuous coalescer" internal functions.
2) Session cache contract: rename internal "context cache" to sessioncache, formalize TTL vs epoch eviction, and add a small pinned-entry set for hot prefixes. Eviction will be moved into a dedicated reaper thread with cooperative backpressure signals.
3) Scheduler handoff: implement an epoched slot descriptor (slot_epoch, token) and transition from heavy spinlocks to an atomic ring descriptor plus lightweight CAS on head/tail pointers. This reduces wakeups and contention on the global ingress mutex.
4) Dependency updates: bump abseil to 2024-12, upgrade the internal concurrency util library (remove custom SpinMutex), and replace a small piece of custom allocator code with the allocator shim introduced in runtime-1.19.
5) Observability and metrics: add per-aggregator metrics (group_size_p50/p95/p99), sessioncache_hit_ratio, eviction_rate, slot_handoff_latency histogram. Expose dashboards and alerts for regressions.

Acceptance criteria/Test plan:
- Unit tests for StreamingAggregator semantics: grouping boundaries, commit callback ordering, and failure handling.
- Integration tests: end-to-end with real inference models under synthetic load; compare p50/p95/p99 latency and throughput with baseline.
- Perf target: p99 tail latency <= baseline + 5ms and throughput >= baseline * 1.05 for the same instance type in 8/16 concurrency profiles. Memory overhead increase <= 7%.
- Canary rollout plan with a 3-stage ramp: 1% -> 10% -> 100% route-based canary. Auto-rollback trigger on >10% increase in errors or >20% p99 increase.

Risk & mitigations:
- Regression in hotkey eviction correctness: mitigation: additive unit tests and an isolated correctness test harness that replays production traces.
- Unexpected memory growth due to pinned set: mitigation: bounded pinned set size and OOM guard with immediate fallback to LRU eviction.
- Performance regressions from dependency upgrade: mitigation: gate upgrades behind feature flag and keep previous implementation behind a runtime flag for quick rollback.

Rollout artifacts & links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Streaming+Aggregator+and+Sessioncache+Contract (internal)
- Benchmark dashboard: https://grafana.internal.redwood.ai/d/serving/stream-agg-perf (internal)
- Draft PR (split into three): https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/12781, https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/12782, https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/12783
- Perf harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness/tree/stream-agg-experiments

Out-of-scope for this ticket:
- Model adapter-level API changes.
- Global memory allocator rewrite (only small allocator shim usage).

2025-02-18: Spike complete — implemented prototype StreamingAggregator in a feature branch; observed 8% throughput improvement and ~10ms p99 reduction on small tracers. Recorded baseline traces for regression tests.
2025-02-22: Design review with scheduler owners — agreed to epoched slot descriptor approach. Noted concerns about pinned set upper bound; added bounded-pinned-set to acceptance criteria.

2025-03-03: Split PRs opened (12781/12782/12783). Initial CI run passes unit tests; integration benchmark run scheduled for 2025-03-05. Feedback from infra: add more traces around slot handoff latency.
2025-03-04: Aisha added implementation for sessioncache reaper and local stress tests. Next: run perf harness across instance types and draft canary runbook.
